# Doc 3a — MCP Server

> **Recovered to the vault 2026-07-29.** This spec governs nine files in the substrate engine and
> is cited 22 times across them, including two verbatim quotations in test docstrings — and it
> existed on no disk anyone could reach. Searched and not found: `~/OneDrive/vaults` (all scopes),
> `~/vaults`, the iCloud Obsidian tree, the CallTranscriber repo, Google Drive, Dropbox. The
> engine was implementing a governing document no future session could read.
>
> **It lives in the PROJECT vault, not core-vault**, deliberately. Doc 1 and Doc 2 are in
> core-vault because several consumers share them and none owns them. Doc 3a describes one
> product's MCP surface and changes as that product changes, so it belongs where changing project
> knowledge belongs.
>
> Verified against the implementation on recovery. **All 22 citations are accurate and both
> verbatim quotes match word-for-word** — the engine did not misquote it. Four divergences were
> found and are marked inline below as `[DIVERGENCE …]`, each with the evidence. None was silently
> edited away.

The product's MCP surface. One server, exposing the brain as tools to any MCP client
(Claude, Zed, Desktop, CLI-adjacent agents).

**Why now:** the engine is built, the result contract is structured, and MCP is a thin
adapter over an interface that already exists. This makes the brain *usable today*,
without waiting on Doc 3's UI work. Everything expensive was already paid for.

**Scope note:** Scripta and the engine are one PRODUCT (the user downloads one thing) but
not one PROCESS — the engine is Python, the app is Swift, the app is a client of the
engine. So the MCP surface phases by what can serve it:

| phase | tools | backed by | state |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | retrieval, scope, ingest, capability | Python engine | **buildable now** |
| 2 | calls, transcripts, recordings, app state | Swift app | later — needs the app to expose them |

Phase 2 lands on the SAME server as additional tools. Starting engine-only forecloses
nothing.

---

## 1. Design principles (inherited, not re-derived)

- **One contract, N renderings.** MCP is a thin adapter over the existing
  `RetrievalResult`. It does not define its own result shape, and it does not put logic
  in the transport. If the MCP adapter needs to compute something, that belongs in the
  engine.
- **Payload discipline: snippet-first.** Return citation + ~200 chars + an `expand_ref`,
  not full passages. Full 1500-char passages × 5 ≈ 2k tokens per query; snippet-first is
  ~5× cheaper. Expansion is a separate tool call, on demand. This is transport-independent
  discipline that MCP makes newly important, because a model caller pays for every token.
- **The capability envelope crosses the boundary.** `retrieval_mode` (which arms actually
  ran, `expected_mrr` or honest `None`) and `index_version` are returned as **structured
  fields**, not prose. A model caller must be able to tell a 0.698-stack answer from a
  0.343 lexical-only one. An applied filter or a degraded arm the consumer can't see is
  the Boundary Principle violated one level down — the same failure the envelope was built
  to fix inside the engine.
- **Refuse rather than mislead.** Hard-fail conditions stay hard-fail across MCP: stale
  index, unavailable required arm, malformed scope. Return an error, not plausible
  degraded results.

> **[DIVERGENCE 4 — vocabulary, unresolved 2026-07-29]** This section calls the field
> `retrieval_mode`, and the wire key IS `retrieval_mode` (`render.py:273`) — spec and code agree.
> The outlier is the repo's own glossary: `substrate/CLAUDE.md:33` reserves `capability` as the
> name for the retrieval-stack state, and SESSION-HANDOFF calls it "the capability envelope".
> Renaming the wire field is a breaking envelope change that ages out every running MCP client;
> dropping `capability` from the glossary is nearly free. **Not decided.**

---

## 2. Tool surface (phase 1)

Minimal and orthogonal. Resist adding tools that are parameter variants of each other.

| tool | purpose | returns |
|---|---|---|
| `search` | query the brain in a given scope | snippet-first passages + outline records + capability + index_version |
| `expand` | fetch full text for an `expand_ref` | the full passage, with path + provenance |
| `list_scopes` | what vaults/scopes exist and what each inherits | scope names + manifest-resolved sources |
| `ingest` | add a markdown/PDF source to a vault | ingestion result + assertion outcomes |
| `status` | index freshness, capability, corpus counts | index_version, per-scope doc counts, current tier |

Notes:
- `search` takes a scope (which vault context), an optional `doc_type` filter, and an
  optional `include_sources` flag (to reach conversation-class and archived content that
  is excluded by default).
- **Default exclusions must be surfaced in the response**, not silently applied — mirror
  the CLI's `status filter: active,complete · sources excluded (--include-sources)` line
  as a structured field. A caller that doesn't know content was withheld will conclude it
  doesn't exist.
- `ingest` over MCP is a **write**. It requires explicit confirmation from the human in
  the loop; it is not a fire-and-forget tool call. Additive-only (new sources); it never
  edits existing notes — that path is diff-gated per Doc 4a's write model.

> **[DIVERGENCE 1 — the ENGINE is behind this spec, 2026-07-29]** "an optional `doc_type` filter"
> is specified here and is NOT implemented: `search` refuses the argument —
> *"There is no doc_type filter — filter the returned passages yourself"* (`mcp/server.py:162`).
> The refusal is honest rather than wrong (it does not return unfiltered results under a filtered
> label), but the axis ships without the filter this section promises. **Decide: implement it, or
> narrow this line.** Note the earlier SESSION-HANDOFF recorded this backwards, as "Doc 3a
> describes a `doc_type` filter that refuses".

> **[DIVERGENCE 2 — this spec is WRONG, the engine is right, 2026-07-29]** One `include_sources`
> flag covering both conversation-class AND archived content folds two independent axes into one.
> The engine keeps them separate — `include_sources` (class) and `include_archived` (status),
> `mcp/server.py:173` and `:182`. Doc 2 §6c is the argument for why they cannot merge: superseded
> content is excluded because it was REPLACED, a conversation because per-passage retrieval
> MISREPRESENTS a document still wanted whole — and the two therefore disagree about embedding.
> A caller given one flag cannot ask for one without the other. **This section should be corrected
> to two flags; the engine needs no change.**

> **[DIVERGENCE 3 — this spec overstates, 2026-07-29]** `ingest` is described as taking a
> "markdown/PDF source". The engine deliberately refuses PDFs over MCP and routes them to the CLI
> (`mcp/server.py:475`): *"PDF ingestion does not run through this tool… use `ingest --pdf` and
> place the reviewed output deliberately."* **This row should read markdown only.**

---

## 3. Scope selection — how the server knows which vaults

The manifest already answers this (Doc 2 §2): a vault declares `inherits`, the engine
composes core + project at retrieval. Over MCP, scope is a **parameter**, not server
config — one server serves all scopes, and the caller names the one it wants.

- `list_scopes` lets a client discover them.
- A client with directory context (Zed in a project) can pass the matching scope.
- **Scope resolution failure hard-fails.** If `inherits` can't resolve, refuse — do NOT
  silently fall back to project-only. A query that quietly drops the core tier and returns
  plausible project-only results is the chapter-title bug wearing a new hat.

*Implemented as specified — `scopes.py`, `cli.py:598`, `mcp/server.py:554`, `test_scopes.py`.*

---

## 4. The idle-cost question

~15 MCP servers are already loaded; each pays context rent every turn. Adding one more is
marginally cheap, but the honest framing (from the transport analysis) is that a
**few-times-a-day tool paying rent every turn is the wrong cost structure** — not because
the rent is high, but because usage is rare relative to payment.

Resolution:
- **Prefer deferred/progressive loading** where the platform supports it (defer_loading, a
  gateway, tool_search). This is the actual fix for idle tax — not payload tricks.
- Keep the tool surface **small** (five tools, above). Fewer tools = less resident schema.
- Skill+CLI remains the better fit for Claude Code specifically (~20 tokens until
  invoked). MCP earns its place for surfaces with no shell — Desktop, web, Zed's agent.
- Both are thin adapters over the same contract, so "both" is not duplication: the logic
  lives in the engine, the adapters are transport only.

---

## 5. What this server is NOT

- **Not a second implementation.** No retrieval logic, no filtering rules, no ranking in
  the adapter. If the MCP path can return something the CLI can't, the logic leaked.
- **Not an orchestration layer.** Arranging the other ~15 servers is Doc 4b, a separate
  and deliberately-scoped concern. This server is one well-behaved citizen among them —
  by the query-not-dump standard, already the best-behaved one.
- **Not a write channel for note edits.** Additive ingest only. In-place edits to existing
  notes go through diff-review (Doc 4a); the MCP server does not bypass that gate.

---

## 6. Build order

1. `search` + `expand` over the existing `RetrievalResult` — the two that make the brain
   usable. Snippet-first from the start; retrofitting payload discipline is harder than
   building it in.
2. `list_scopes` + `status` — discovery and honesty. `status` is what lets a caller notice
   a stale index rather than silently querying one.
3. `ingest` — with human-confirmation, once 1–2 are proven.
4. Phase 2 (app-backed tools) when Scripta exposes them.

**Verification:** an MCP `search` and the equivalent CLI query must return the same
passages, same capability, same index_version for the same scope. If they diverge, logic
leaked into a transport. That equivalence is the test that keeps "one contract, N
renderings" true rather than aspirational.

*All four build-order steps are shipped. The verification is
`test_mcp_server.test_mcp_and_cli_render_the_same_envelope`, which runs the real CLI in a
subprocess and the real tool handler in-process and compares the parsed envelopes as whole dicts.
An earlier version asserted five named keys and passed while the two adapters emitted structurally
different envelopes — assert the whole object, not a subset.*

---

## Open

- Whether `expand` returns the full passage or the whole note (connective questions may
  want the note; Doc 2's small-tier expansion path suggests both, gated by a parameter).
- Auth/isolation if the server is ever reachable beyond localhost — out of scope today
  (localhost only), but the loopback-guard work is the relevant precedent.
- Phase 2's app-backed tool surface — undefined until Scripta exposes an interface.

> **[CLOSED 2026-07-29 — the first Open item]** `expand` gained exactly the parameter this
> question anticipated: `mode="passage"|"note"`, where `note` returns the whole note with a
> staleness verdict (`mcp/server.py:199`, `:208`, `:339`). The answer was "both, gated by a
> parameter". The question was answered by the implementation and the spec never learned.
>
> The other two remain open. The loopback guard named as precedent for the second is built
> (`tests/test_loopback_guard.py`).
